title: Crawlers from noise in a 4x larger box (L=10, 512^2, area fraction 0.25): 20-24 layered cells, several crawlers from t~4, but absorption keeps going (24 -> 11 and 21 -> 6 bodies by t=14), so a bigger box does not lengthen merger-free runs
summary: World of 20261026T0406-c31-crawlers-from-noise-claim with L=10, N=512 (same dx), area fraction 0.25, seeds 0-1, t=14 (pathprobe_big.py). By t~4, 20-24 round cells with their own s rings form, and 3-4 of them are polarized half-moon crawlers among static disks (big_fig.png). Crawlers then absorb disks and each other: bodies fall from 24 to 11 (seed 0) and from 21 to 6 (seed 1), and the largest body grows to cover a large part of the box. Merger-free stretches (the body count is constant anywhere in the box, so the measure is conservative) last at most 2.5 time units and give at most 0.42 own diameters (segments.txt), with the largest body moving at 0.23-0.67. So the earlier box-size reading (20261026T0449-c31-noise-crawler-path) was wrong: crawlers keep meeting other cells in a larger box too, and absorption, not box size, limits their free runs. A sparser start leaves cells below the polarity window, so M from noise would need cells that repel or bounce instead of fusing.
